turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, the Wednesday. I'm writing those down. People draft in one place and paste it into another, so was Owen asked a single question before that zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
You still haven't answered me: was Owen heard before you entered that zero? And whatever happens from here, this stays off his record and it stays out of his classroom.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day. Turn it, I'll search it myself. If it isn't there, tell me exactly what you're proposing, because I'm not leaving with a zero and nothing else.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
Fine, it isn't there. Put your offer on the table, and it had better be private, and it had better keep him off any record.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a take-home essay with the play open are not the same thing, and you know it, Hale. I've read them both. I'm still waiting for your offer.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Okay, to put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite. In tonight's email I want 4.4 spelled out: private, supervised, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, and your apology for how he found out. I'll be reading it before I sleep.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. You get the email to me tonight, and you tell me the date and time of the rewrite in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's Hamlet essay under procedure 4.4, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require those terms in writing, together with your apology for entering the zero before anyone contacted me and the date and time of the rewrite. You said I would have it tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero. She still wants the terms, your apology and the rewrite's date and time in writing tonight. That is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by inviting her to bring the other file, because every point was dated and checkable and left her no room to argue.
What cost ground: Nothing; you never leaned on the detector score, never called Owen a liar, and never offered the rewrite before you had shown your evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the Wednesday night before it was due, very close to the kind of night she saw; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she twice asked whether Owen had been heard before the zero went in, answer that directly instead of moving to your next document, so she has no unanswered process question to take upstairs.
